value: A counts Sunday, which is never a business day for rescission. C wrongly drops Saturday, which counts under the precise rule. D has no basis: the right lasts three business days, not a week.
reason: The old text said A 'skips Saturday' and D 'uses calendar days'. Monday is what you get by counting Sunday (Saturday, Sunday, Monday), and three calendar days would also give Monday, not the following Friday. § 1026.2(a)(6): 'all calendar days except Sundays and the legal public holidays'.

value: A: only four business days (Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Monday) will have passed. C: that ignores Saturday, which counts as a business day here. D: that is later than necessary.
reason: From a Wednesday hand-over, Monday is the fourth business day when Saturday counts, not the third. Comment 19(e)(1)(iii)-2: 'Saturday is a business day, pursuant to § 1026.2(a)(6)'.

value: If the consumer pays a loan originator directly, nobody else may pay a loan originator on that loan, except a firm paying its own staff.
reason: 'No one else may pay a loan originator' overstates the rule and contradicts the card dual-comp-org-pays-lo. § 1026.36(d)(2)(i)(C): 'the loan originator organization may pay compensation to an individual loan originator'.

value: The ban stops a loan originator being paid twice for one loan. Section 1026.36(d)(2)(i)(C) still lets a consumer-paid firm pay its own individual loan originators, but not on the terms of the loan.
reason: The old explanation ('rules out every other source of pay') repeated the overstatement. § 1026.36(d)(2)(i)(C) allows the firm to pay its individual loan originator 'subject to paragraph (d)(1)'.

value: That is the general rule. If the transfer follows events such as the servicer's bankruptcy or the servicing contract being ended for cause, either notice may come up to 30 days after the effective date.
reason: The back gives the general rule as if it had no exceptions. § 1024.33(b)(3)(ii): 'not more than 30 days after the effective date of the transfer ... in any case in which the transfer of servicing is preceded by' termination for cause, bankruptcy or FDIC/NCUA proceedings.

value: The appraiser must physically visit the interior, so a drive-by or desktop valuation will not do. Some loans are exempt under § 1026.35(c)(2), including qualified mortgages.
reason: The card presented the rule as covering every HPML. § 1026.35(c)(3)(i) opens 'Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2)', and (c)(2)(i) exempts 'A loan that satisfies the criteria of a qualified mortgage'.

value: If settlement is expected over 60 days after the Loan Estimate, which clearly warned that revised disclosures may come until 60 days before consummation.
reason: 'The original said so clearly' reads as if the Loan Estimate had to predict the late settlement. What it must state is that revised disclosures may be issued up to 60 days before consummation. § 1026.19(e)(3)(iv)(F): 'state clearly and conspicuously that at any time prior to 60 days before consummation, the creditor may issue revised disclosures'.

value: Without that warning on the original Loan Estimate this ground is not available, because new-construction settlements often run late and the consumer must be told costs may be revised.
reason: Follows the corrected back. § 1026.19(e)(3)(iv)(F), 'Delayed settlement date on a construction loan'.

value: A and B are true of her, but they are not enough: her balance is still above 80 percent of the original value. D is wrong: the escrow can be cancelled on request once every condition is met.
reason: 'A and B each meet only one condition' is confusing: the borrower meets both the five-year and the current-payment conditions, and the one she fails is the 80 percent test. § 1026.35(b)(3)(ii)(A)-(B).

value: A step-by-step booklet from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau for people buying a home.
reason: The toolkit names its publisher 'Consumer Financial Protection Bureau' (and calls itself 'A step-by-step guide'). 'Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection' appears nowhere in it and would puzzle a newcomer who has met only 'CFPB'.
